title: Context Parallelism for Scalable Million-Token Inference
technique: context parallelism with lossless ring attention (pass-KV / pass-Q) and load-balanced sharding for long-context prefill and decode

optimized_metrics.evidence: Latency is critical for user experience in real-time inference. To optimize latency in multi-turn conversations, we developed pass-KV and pass-Q ring attention variants
optimized_metrics.stat_note: figure axis label for the prefill latency scaling plots (txt lines 630, 665); text does not otherwise state a statistic

headline_claim.text: 1M context prefill with Llama3 405B model in 77s (93% parallelization efficiency, 63% FLOPS utilization) and 128K context prefill in 3.8s

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Time-to-first-token: latency for prefilling the whole input tokens
metric_definitions.notes: Pure prefill latency (batch size 1); no queueing.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Time-to-incremental-token: latency for decoding each output token
metric_definitions.notes: Paper's own name for TBT/TPOT; reported in ms.

load_regime: batch size 1 per configuration; sweep over context length (128K-1M) and KV-cache miss rate; no request arrivals
tradeoff_acknowledged: Explicit: 'CP drastically improves the prefill latency, at the expense of decode latency regression'; TTIT 47 ms for TP scaling vs growth with CP.
hardware: up to 16 nodes x 8 H100 (Grand Teton Training, RDMA; Grand Teton Inference, TCP)
workloads: synthetic long prompts; multi-turn partial prefill (persistent KV)
extractor_notes: Single-request latency study; no throughput or tail metric. Uses 'TTIT' rather than TPOT/TBT.
load_class_quote: "We used max batch size 1 and tested how the full prefill latency for context lengths 2K to 128K vary with respect to the addition of more CP nodes." (§4.2.1, txt line 558-559)
repass_log: duplicate TTFT entry (abstract result quote) merged into the design entry (§1 'Optimization for latency')
remaining TTFT: design; stat_basis explicit only via 'Average Latency (s)' axis label (weak)
